## Definitions

- [statement] LiteLLM exposes /v1/messages and an Anthropic-format SDK entry point for non-Anthropic providers; endpoint availability does not imply lossless Anthropic feature parity. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/anthropic_unified · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, /v1/messages, Anthropic, LiteLLM, Messages · also: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/anthropic_unified/native_passthrough

## Structure and components

- [fact] The Chat bridge maps client-tool input_schema into OpenAI function parameters; the schema describes arguments, while tool execution stays with the client application. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/llms/anthropic/pass_through/adapters/transformation.py · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, Chat, input_schema, tool · also: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls

## How it works

- [fact] The Chat bridge maps assistant tool_use blocks to function tool_calls and user tool_result blocks to role=tool messages, preserving call/result correlation through id and tool_call_id. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/llms/anthropic/pass_through/adapters/transformation.py · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, Chat, Messages, tool, tool_call_id, tool_calls · also: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls
- [fact] On the Chat return path, LiteLLM reconstructs tool_use blocks from structured tool_calls and maps finish_reason=tool_calls to stop_reason=tool_use. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/llms/anthropic/pass_through/adapters/transformation.py · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, Chat, LiteLLM, finish_reason, stop_reason, tool_calls · also: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls
- [fact] For client function tools, the application executes each selected call and returns its result; generating a tool block does not perform the operation. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/handle-tool-calls · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, function-tool, tool · also: https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/tool-calling, https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/tool_calling/

## Parameters and configuration

- [statement] The Chat adapter maps Anthropic tool_choice any to required, auto to auto, tool to a named function, and none to none; downstream support remains a separate check. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/llms/anthropic/pass_through/adapters/transformation.py · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, Anthropic, Chat, tool, tool_choice
- [statement] At the inspected commit, openai/ Messages requests use Responses by default. For a chat-only target, use_chat_completions_url_for_anthropic_messages selects the Chat bridge instead. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/llms/anthropic/pass_through/messages/handler.py · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, Chat, Messages, Responses, use_chat_completions_url_for_anthropic_messages · also: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/config_settings
- [statement] If the upstream implements Messages natively, model_info.supported_endpoints can opt into /v1/messages passthrough; ordinary OpenAI compatibility alone is insufficient for that opt-in. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/anthropic_unified/native_passthrough · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, /v1/messages, Messages, passthrough, supported_endpoints · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/llms/anthropic/pass_through/messages/handler.py

## How-to and procedures

- [fact] LiteLLM's Chat-stream wrapper emits Anthropic block lifecycle events and input_json_delta fragments. Clients must assemble tool arguments by block and wait for closure before parsing them. — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/llms/anthropic/pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, Anthropic, LiteLLM, input_json_delta, tool · also: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/messages-streaming
- [fact] Verify native function-tool capability and model-specific parsing before using a translated local backend for agent work; an API wrapper cannot supply missing model competence. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers/ollama · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, function-tool · also: https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/tool_calling/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [fact] Treat initial HTTP 200 as provisional for streamed generation: Anthropic errors can arrive in SSE after headers, and LiteLLM's Messages router explicitly handles stream error events. — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/errors · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, Anthropic, HTTP 200, LiteLLM, Messages, stream · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/82d8b3797cf124e2baaa9c342f87a57fbb3a1a96/litellm/router.py
- [statement] Translation can approximate or lose Anthropic-only details. Native passthrough also reduces cache_control to its portable core unless cache_control_ttl is enabled; avoid promising byte-for-byte fidelity. — https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/anthropic_unified/native_passthrough · keywords: LiteLLM Anthropic Messages interoperability, cache_control_ttl, passthrough
